q1_issues.issue: Past wraps only the locative relation while the same past clause's typing atoms stay unwrapped, contradicting the mechanical rule that a past copular clause wraps every categorical atom it yields.
'a pile of firewood' is rendered by predicating the mass kind of the pile itself, asserting that the pile IS firewood rather than relating the aggregate to its material.

q2_gaps: container / aggregate 'N of MASS' ('a pile of firewood', 'a cup of water') — the genitive section explicitly excludes it from Possession but supplies no positive form, and it is neither a partitive 'of the' nor a numbered Measure
tense on an existential 'there was/were' clause — the Existential section's examples are present-tense only and never say which of the clause's atoms take the past wrapper
notes: NextTo is licensed as an entity-attached preposition-named relation, on the pattern of (From sk_wool_1 calderwick) and (Beside sk_fountain_1 sk_archive_1), and reifying no event is correct for 'there was' plus a static locative.
